poems.title: Thick-Sprinkled Bunting
poems.heading: THICK-SPRINKLED BUNTING
poems.first: Thick-sprinkled bunting! flag of stars!
poems.last: Flag of stars! thick-sprinkled bunting!

poems.title: Beat! Beat! Drums!
poems.heading: BEAT! BEAT! DRUMS!
poems.first: Beat! beat! drums!—blow! bugles! blow!
poems.last: So strong you thump O terrible drums—so loud you bugles blow.

poems.title: City of Ships
poems.heading: CITY OF SHIPS
poems.first: City of ships!
poems.last: War, red war is my song through your streets, O city!

poems.title: A March in the Ranks Hard-Prest, and the Road Unknown
poems.heading: A MARCH IN THE RANKS HARD-PREST, AND THE ROAD UNKNOWN
poems.first: A march in the ranks hard-prest, and the road unknown,
poems.last: The unknown road still marching.

poems.title: Come Up from the Fields Father
poems.heading: COME UP FROM THE FIELDS FATHER
poems.first: Come up from the fields father, here's a letter from our Pete,
poems.last: To follow, to seek, to be with her dear dead son.

poems.title: A Twilight Song
poems.heading: A TWILIGHT SONG
poems.first: As I sit in twilight late alone by the flickering oak-flame,
poems.last: Embalm'd with love in this twilight song.

poems.title: A Sight in Camp in the Daybreak Gray and Dim
poems.heading: A SIGHT IN CAMP IN THE DAYBREAK GRAY AND DIM
poems.first: A sight in camp in the daybreak gray and dim,
poems.last: Dead and divine and brother of all, and here again he lies.

poems.title: Year That Trembled and Reel'd Beneath Me
poems.heading: YEAR THAT TREMBLED AND REEL'D BENEATH ME
poems.first: Year that trembled and reel'd beneath me!
poems.last: And sullen hymns of defeat?

poems.title: Old War-Dreams
poems.heading: OLD WAR-DREAMS
poems.first: In midnight sleep of many a face of anguish,
poems.last: I dream, I dream, I dream.

poems.title: Delicate Cluster
poems.heading: DELICATE CLUSTER
poems.first: Delicate cluster! flag of teeming life!
poems.last: My sacred one, my mother!

poems.title: To a Certain Civilian
poems.heading: TO A CERTAIN CIVILIAN
poems.first: Did you ask dulcet rhymes from me?
poems.last: For I lull nobody, and you will never understand me.

poems.title: Adieu to a Soldier
poems.heading: ADIEU TO A SOLDIER
poems.first: Adieu O soldier,
poems.last: To fiercer, weightier battles give expression.

poems.title: Long, Too Long America
poems.heading: LONG, TOO LONG AMERICA
poems.first: Long, too long America,
poems.last: (For who except myself has yet conceiv'd what your children en-masse really are?).

poems.title: Weave In, My Hardy Life
poems.heading: WEAVE IN, MY HARDY LIFE
poems.first: Weave in, weave in, my hardy life,
poems.last: We know not why or what, yet weave, forever weave.

poems.title: Spirit Whose Work Is Done
poems.heading: SPIRIT WHOSE WORK IS DONE
poems.first: Spirit whose work is done—spirit of dreadful hours!
poems.last: Let them identify you to the future in these songs.

poems.title: O Captain! My Captain!
poems.heading: O CAPTAIN! MY CAPTAIN!
poems.first: O Captain! my Captain! our fearful trip is done,
poems.last: Fallen cold and dead.

poems.title: Hush'd Be the Camps To-Day
poems.heading: HUSH'D BE THE CAMPS TO-DAY
poems.first: Hush'd be the camps to-day,
poems.last: For the heavy hearts of soldiers.

poems.title: I Hear America Singing
poems.heading: I HEAR AMERICA SINGING
poems.first: I hear America singing, the varied carols I hear,
poems.last: Singing with open mouths their strong melodious songs.

poems.title: To Foreign Lands
poems.heading: TO FOREIGN LANDS
poems.first: I heard that you ask'd for something to prove this puzzle the New World,
poems.last: Therefore I send you my poems that you behold in them what you wanted.

poems.title: For You O Democracy
poems.heading: FOR YOU O DEMOCRACY
poems.first: Come, I will make the continent indissoluble,
poems.last: For you, for you I am trilling these songs.
